summary: Tillamook County, OR tower site administered by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry; built 1940 after the 1933 burn; removed 1956 or 1960, sources differ; no current description.

facts.design: 40-foot L-4 tower; sources differ on pole or timber construction
facts.status_note: Removed in 1956 or 1960 (sources differ); no source we read describes what remains on the butte today

events.note: Newspaper report quoted on Forest Lookouts page: a lookout would be established on Edwards Butte in the southwestern part of the 1933 burned area
40-foot L-4 tower built; the register says pole, Forest Lookouts says timber; cab reported as 14x14 (no unit given)
Activated March 9, 1942, per Forest Lookouts page, which also names the Portland Filter Center in the same entry
Register says removed in 1956; firelookout.com says destroyed 1956
Forest Lookouts page gives 1960 as the removal year; conflicts with the 1956 date
Registered November 8, 2010 as FFLOS US 705, OR 116; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: administered by the Oregon Department of Forestry

evidence.quote: In 1940, a 40' pole L-4 tower was built, which was removed in 1956.

evidence.supports: 1940 40-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1956 per firelookout.com
location nine miles southeast of Tillamook
Forest Log 1940: lookout tower on Edwards Butte nine miles west of Camp Trask
evidence.quote: nine miles west of Camp Trask

evidence.quote: A lookout would be established on Edwards Butte in the southwestern section of the 1933 burned area.

The tower is forty feet high.

evidence.quote: 1940: A 40-foot timber tower with a 14x14 cab completed.

evidence.supports: activation date March 9, 1942 and Portland Filter Center in the same entry

notes_for_editor: Built 1940 is consistent across all three pages. Removal year conflicts: register says 1956 'removed', firelookout.com says 'Destroyed 1956', Forest Lookouts page says '1960: Removed'; story reports all three without choosing. Location conflicts: firelookout.com says nine miles southeast of Tillamook; the 1940 Forest Log quote on the Forest Lookouts page says nine miles west of Camp Trask. Construction material differs (pole vs timber). The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1936 newspaper (Daily Capital Journal) and a 1937 annual report, both cited through that page, not read directly. The register page carries a 2010 photo credited to Howard Verschoor; image URL and licence were not captured, so no photo entry. No source describes the site today or public access. One web search run; nothing new found. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1936 newspaper sentence in the story is now paraphrased rather than quoted; the October 1940 date and the crew cabin have quotes; the 14x14 cab is given without a unit because the page gives none.
